Done: POST
/v1/transfers/{consumerPid}/completion" style="endArrow=blockThin;endFill=1;html=1;rounded=0;strokeColor=#606060;fontSize=11;fontColor=#404040;labelBackgroundColor=#FFFFFF;verticalAlign=bottom;" edge="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"><mxPoint x="120" y="1533.5" as="sourcePoint" /><mxPoint x="610" y="1533.5" as="targetPoint" /><mxPoint x="120" y="-3" as="offset" /></mxGeometry></mxCell><mxCell id="m30_cc_pc_1576" value="30. POST /transfers/{providerPid}/completion:
TransferCompletionMessage" style="endArrow=blockThin;endFill=1;html=1;rounded=0;strokeColor=#606060;fontSize=11;fontColor=#404040;labelBackgroundColor=#FFFFFF;verticalAlign=bottom;" edge="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"><mxPoint x="610" y="1576" as="sourcePoint" /><mxPoint x="980" y="1576" as="targetPoint" /><mxPoint x="0" y="-3" as="offset" /></mxGeometry></mxCell><mxCell id="foot" value="C4 model, dynamic diagram. Numbers give the order; dashed arrows are answers. Every DSP message, either way, carries a new token from the sender's STS and is checked like 4 to 7 (callbacks by the consumer, against the provider's identity); those calls are drawn only for the first. Each connector saves a message before sending it and sends it again after a restart (ADR 0007). The catalog request is not saved: it is sent once, and the consumer's connector hands on the provider's answer as it came. From 1.1 (ADR 0027) the provider checks the consumer's membership again at 25 and while 28 runs, cuts 28 when the transfer is suspended or terminated, and writes the audit line data transfer done when 28 ends. A source may also be s3://{bucket}/{key} in the provider's object storage, read with a signed GET. Push transfers (HttpData-PUSH) are not drawn: there the provider's data plane POSTs the data to the consumer's /push/{consumerPid}." style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontStyle=0;fontColor=#555555;whiteSpace=wrap;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="20" y="1632" width="1540" height="63" as="geometry" /></mxCell></root></mxGraphModel></diagram></mxfile>
svg.text: Dynamic: negotiating a contract and transferring data
A consumer and a provider, each a portitor-connector with its portitor-identity: catalog, contract negotiation to FINALIZED and a pull transfer (DSP 2025-1), every DSP request checked with DCP
7. Caller check (ADR 0016): ID token against the caller's DID
document; presentation and credentials; issuer in
PORTITOR_TRUSTED_ISSUERS; status list bit not set
13. Caller check as in 4 to 7. Offer is the catalog's; its
permissions hold now for this caller (dateTime, credential
constraints: more scopes, ADR 0019); saves REQUESTED,
21. Caller check; a FINALIZED agreement held by the caller
whose permissions hold (a request that comes before the
acknowledgement of 17 proves that 17 arrived, ADR 0007);
the data plane starts a flow with a new bearer token (only its
hash is kept) and keeps the caller's memberships with it
23. Keeps the data address, token included,
2. POST /sts/token: ID token for the provider
9. 200: the Catalog as the provider sent it
28. The body, streamed with its Content-Type

C4 model, dynamic diagram. Numbers give the order; dashed arrows are answers. Every DSP message, either way, carries a new token from the sender's STS and is checked like 4 to 7 (callbacks by the consumer, against the provider's identity); those calls are drawn only for the first. Each connector saves a
message before sending it and sends it again after a restart (ADR 0007). The catalog request is not saved: it is sent once, and the consumer's connector hands on the provider's answer as it came.

From 1.1 (ADR 0027) the provider checks the consumer's membership again at 25 and while 28 runs, cuts 28 when the transfer is suspended or terminated, and writes the audit line data transfer done when 28 ends.

A source may also be s3://{bucket}/{key} in the provider's object storage, read with a signed GET. Push transfers (HttpData-PUSH) are not drawn: there the provider's data plane POSTs the data to the consumer's /push/{consumerPid}.
